logline: Newly released ex-convict Shadow Moon is recruited by the mysterious Mr. Wednesday into a hidden America where ancient gods wage a survival war against the new deities of technology, media, and globalisation.

renewal.note: Starz cancelled American Gods after Season 3 in March 2021. The series ended without a planned finale, leaving the Neil Gaiman adaptation incomplete.

bollymeter.basis: Season 1 earned a 92-percent Rotten Tomatoes score on the strength of Bryan Fuller and Michael Green's visually audacious direction and Ian McShane's career-best small-screen work. Critics described it as one of the most distinctive premieres of 2017.

pull_quotes.text: McShane, giving the runaway performance highlight of the series, does his best to charm us into submission.

seasons.review_body: The debut season of American Gods was a critical event. Bryan Fuller and Michael Green brought Neil Gaiman's novel to Starz with a visual grammar unlike anything else on television - each 'Coming to America' vignette a short film in its own right, the main narrative a road-movie through a mythologically haunted heartland. Ian McShane's Mr. Wednesday is one of television's great magnetic presences, and Ricky Whittle's Shadow provides the grounded perspective through which Gaiman's baroque cosmology lands. The 92-percent Rotten Tomatoes score reflected how decisively Season 1 announced its intent. The show moved like a fever dream and trusted its audience to follow.

episode_reviews.title: The Bone Orchard
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes American Gods as something genuinely strange: a road trip through mythological America, with Ian McShane as a god-shaped con man and a Viking prologue that is pure cinema. Fuller and Green set the show's visual ambition immediately.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The brutal Norse landing sequence - pure aesthetic provocation that tells the audience exactly what kind of show this is.

critic_note.text: A strong opening salvo for American Gods, thanks to the strong dramatic interplay between Ian McShane and Ricky Whittle.

bollymeter.basis: After Fuller and Green departed, Season 2 dropped to 61 percent on Rotten Tomatoes. Critics found the visual ambition diminished and the mythology plot stalled. The show's identity became uncertain.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived after showrunners Bryan Fuller and Michael Green departed mid-production, and the seam shows throughout. The 61-percent Rotten Tomatoes score represented a steep fall from the debut. The season retained the show's bombastic visual instincts but lost the propulsive narrative and the magical compression that made Season 1 feel inevitable. The mythological conflict between Old Gods and New Gods - so kinetic in Year 1 - became muddier, and the series seemed uncertain what Shadow Moon's arc was building toward. McShane remained watchable in almost any condition, but the show around him was no longer the same entity.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 loses its showrunners mid-production and the creative coherence goes with them - a significant drop from the debut's 92 percent to 61 percent on Rotten Tomatoes.

bollymeter.basis: Season 3 recovered partially to 74 percent but was cancelled before a conclusion could be written. The unresolved ending leaves the season as an incomplete chapter rather than a satisfying arc.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 made a partial recovery - 74 percent on Rotten Tomatoes against Season 2's 61 - but was cancelled by Starz before it could resolve the narrative. The season moved Shadow to the fictional town of Lakeside in Minnesota and attempted to recapture the intimate character-study quality of early Season 1. The 74-percent score signals a genuine improvement, though the season remained burdened by unresolved mythology threads accumulated over three years. The abrupt cancellation means American Gods ends without closure - a frustrating outcome for a show that once felt like it might be the fantasy drama of its generation.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 3 partially rebounds in quality but is cancelled mid-story, leaving the adaptation permanently incomplete.
